edits.english: Further regarding a court ruling that involves uprooting a mitzva, Rav Yosef raises a dilemma: If the court issued a ruling that there is no prohibition against plowing on Shabbat, what is the halakha? The Gemara elaborates: Do we say that since the judges agree to the application of the entire matter of prohibitions on Shabbat and their ruling is exclusively with regard to plowing, its status is tantamount to nullification of a portion of the mitzva and fulfillment of a portion of the mitzva? Or perhaps, since the judges are abolishing the principal category of labor of plowing in its entirety, it is tantamount to abolishing the essence of the mitzva of Shabbat.

Rav Yosef raises a dilemma: There is no plowing on Shabbat, what is it? - Here, Rav Yosef's dilemma is not concerning a matter that the Sadducees do not agree with at all; rather, his dilemma is regarding nullification of a portion and fulfillment of a portion.

edits.hebrew: מי אמרינן כיון דקא מודו - בית דין בכולהו שאר מלאכות דשבת דאסירי, כביטול מקצת וקיום מקצת דמי וחייבין:

edits.english: א And further regarding a court ruling that involves uprooting a mitzva. Rav Yosef asked: If the court ruled that there is no prohibition against plowing on Shabbat, what is the halakha? And the sides of the question are: Do we say: Since they agree to the entire matter, to all Shabbat prohibitions, and their ruling is only concerning plowing, this is considered like nullification of a portion and fulfillment of a portion? Or perhaps, since they are uprooting the labor of plowing entirely, this is considered like uprooting the essence of the mitzva of Shabbat?

Rashi wrote that this dilemma of Rav Yosef is not a continuation of the previous discussion, but rather a question in itself: If a court ruled to permit one of the labors of Shabbat entirely, is it considered ruling on a portion or nullifying an entire matter?

However, the commentators raise another question: The labor of plowing is explicitly forbidden in the Torah (as it says, "In plowing and in harvest you shall rest"), and therefore it is a matter that the Sadducees agree with, and according to Shmuel, this is not a valid ruling! Tosafot said that regarding plowing itself, Rav Yosef knows that this is not a valid ruling, but he mentioned plowing as an example of one of the labors of Shabbat, and he chose this example because it is listed first in the count of labors. Meiri writes similarly, that regarding plowing, since it is explicit in the Torah, it is certainly not a valid ruling. Indeed, the Rosh believes that Rav Yosef does not accept Shmuel's opinion, and therefore his question is only a continuation of the Mishnah: Is this matter called a partial mitzva or a complete mitzva (and Chafetz Hashem also inclined to this view, and others). Whereas the Rama (cited in the Rosh) believes that even regarding the labor of plowing, the Sadducees do not agree, because they interpret the verse "In plowing and in harvest you shall rest" not as a prohibition on these labors, but "plowing" and "harvest" are, in their opinion, seasons of the year (winter and summer), and they interpret the verse as saying that one must rest from labor in all seasons of the year.

If a court ruled that there is no plowing on Shabbat, they are liable to bring an offering.

See in the Kesef Mishneh and Lechem Mishneh that they labored to explain in various ways how the Rambam solved this problem which remained unresolved in the Gemara. And some wrote that the Rambam had a variant reading later in the Gemara: "Come and hear from Rabbi Zeira's dilemma," meaning that by resolving Rabbi Zeira's dilemma, Rav Yosef's dilemma was also resolved. (Rambam, Sefer Korbanot, Hilkhot Shegagot 14:2).

edits.hebrew: בעי רב יוסף אין חרישה וכולי - רישא דאבות מלאכות דפרק כלל גדול נקט, אבל חרישה צדוקין מודין בה. ולרב יוסף נמי בעי דבר שאין מודין בו, כדלקמן אמר לך רב יוסף וכולי, משמע דסבר כשמואל:

edits.english: (And all of them) as we explained - Above, that it is not considered uprooting the entire essence of the *shomeret yom* (woman who observes a day for a day).
(And all of it) as we explained - That passing and throwing are permitted, as it is not considered uprooting the entire essence.
(And all of it) as we explained - That bowing in an atypical manner is permitted.

edits.hebrew: אמרי [אומרים] בדחיית אותה ראיה: השתחויה נמי כדשנין [גם כן יש לומר כמו שתירצנו מקודם] שהתירו רק בהשתחוויה מעטה, ולא עקרו את כל האיסור.

ועוד בענין הוראת בית דין שיש בה עקירת מצוה. בעי [שאל] ר' זירא: הורו בית הדין שאין איסור שבת בשנה השביעית (שנת השמיטה), מהו? ולפני שמבררים את השאלה, מקדימים ושואלים: במאי [במה] טעו, מה גרם להם לטעות זו? בהדין קרא [בפסוק זה] שנאמר במצות השבת: "בחריש ובקציר תשבת" (שמות לד, כא), והם מפרשים: בזמן דאיכא [שיש] חרישה כלומר, בשאר השנים איכא [יש] איסור שבת, ובזמן דליכא [שאין] חרישה בשנת השמיטה, שאסור לחרוש בה ליכא [אין] איסור שבת נוהג.

edits.english: In plowing and in harvest you shall rest - Which implies: During a time when there is plowing, meaning in the other years of the Sabbatical cycle, there is Shabbat.
During a time when there is no plowing - Meaning, in the Sabbatical Year, there is no Shabbat.

Some sages believe that this question is not related to Rav Yosef's question, but is a different question (on the same topic): Is nullification for a specific time considered partial nullification (Chafetz Hashem, Magen Giborim)? And indeed, this is somewhat implied by the style of the Gemara's words.

However, the Rosh explains it differently, and it appears from his wording that he had a different version: If you were to say that there is no plowing on Shabbat, which is considered uprooting the entire essence and they are exempt, then they said: What is the law if there is no plowing or harvesting on Shabbat during the Sabbatical Year? And according to this version, the ruling of the Rambam (which many wondered about) that resolves Rav Yosef's question is understood, as he ruled according to his custom of "if you were to say."

edits.hebrew: שמע מינה אין שבת בשביעית וכולי - משמע דאין צדוקין מודין בהאי דרשא, אף על גב דלעיל דרשי ליה יהיה לה לשומרת (יבם) [יום]:

edits.english: A prophet who prophesies - For example, one who was initially a true prophet and eventually became a false prophet, who prophesied to uproot a matter from the words of the Torah, is liable, and everyone agrees to strangulation.

edits.hebrew: לקיום מקצת ולבטל מקצת - דשאר מצות רבי שמעון פוטר, והוא הדין לרבנן:

ובעבודת כוכבים אפילו אמר לך היום עובדה ולמחר בטלה - דהיינו קיום מקצת וביטול מקצת דעבודת כוכבים חייב, דרחמנא אמר: להדיחך מן הדרך, אפילו מקצת דרך, ובעבודת כוכבים הוא דכתיב. וכי קתני חייב, כגון לרבנן בסקילה ולרבי שמעון בחנק. והכי מתרץ ליה רב חסדא בפרק אלו הן הנחנקין (סנהדרין דף צ.). והיום עובדה ולמחר בטלה כאין שבת בשביעית דמי, וקרי להו ביטול מקצת וקיום מקצת. שמע מינה:
